# Golden fixtures

Everything here came from somewhere else. Most of it is copied out of the original's committed results without changing a byte, and the rest was produced by running the original's own tools. None of it was measured by this harness and none of it will ever be regenerated by it, because a fixture we produce ourselves proves only that we agree with ourselves.

## Single files

| File | What it pins down |
|---|---|
| `bench_dragonfly-threads_1-pipeline_1-perf_no-run_1.json` | A single run with perf detached, where `perf` has to serialise as `{}` rather than as null or as a missing key |
| `bench_dragonfly-threads_1-pipeline_1-perf_yes-run_1.json` | A single run with perf attached, where every counter is a JSON string, including a `<not supported>` one |
| `bench_dragonfly-threads_1-pipeline_1-perf_yes-run_median.json` | A chosen file, where the same counters are JSON numbers and `kind` has been appended last |
| `output-three-cells.json` | Three complete entries lifted out of the published `output.json`, which pins the combined layout and its odd indentation |

Every one of them is asserted byte for byte in both directions. That is deliberate rather than fussy. The point of matching the original's format is that its published results can be fed to our chart engine and ours to its `graph`, and that cross check stops working the moment a field gets renamed for being nicer.

These are here because they are small. The whole published `output.json` is 1.7 MB of measurement data and does not belong in this repository, so the test that reads it is ignored by default and takes a path in `CB_PARITY_OUTPUT`:

```
CB_PARITY_OUTPUT=/path/to/cache-benchmarks/results/output.json cargo test -p cb-core -- --ignored
```

That one covers all 2304 entries and is the test that catches formatting bugs the three cell fixture is too small to reach.

Set `CB_PARITY_EMIT` as well and it writes what our emitter produced, which is the file to point the original's `graph` at:

```
mkdir -p /tmp/parity/results/graphs
CB_PARITY_OUTPUT=/path/to/cache-benchmarks/results/output.json \
CB_PARITY_EMIT=/tmp/parity/results/output.json \
  cargo test -p cb-core -- --ignored
cd /path/to/cache-benchmarks/cmd && go build -o /tmp/parity/graph ./graph
cd /tmp/parity && ./graph -dir results -bench throughput -which get -pipeline 10 -scale linear -force
```

`graph` needs `python3` with matplotlib, and it warns that it cannot find Futura on anything that is not a Mac with Futura installed. Neither of those is about the data. That is the second half of the M1 exit condition: the original's chart tool reads a file we wrote and draws from it, throughput, latency and cycles alike.

## cells

Two whole cells, both dragonfly at one thread and pipeline depth 1, one measured with perf and one without. Each file holds the 31 runs the original committed and the four files the original reduced them to, gathered into one file per cell so that a repository does not end up holding what looks like a results directory.

They are what the statistics are tested against. Because the answers are in the file next to the question, a test can say that the original's published median GET is rank 16 of 31 where the median is rank 15, rather than saying that our median looks reasonable.

## gosort.json

142 cases produced by Go's `sort.Slice`, which is the one fixture here that is generated rather than copied. Upstream mode has to reproduce the original's SET numbers, and those come out of a sort whose comparator reads a slice it is not sorting, so the result depends on the exact sequence of comparisons and swaps rather than on the values. Matching it means matching Go's `pdqsort`, and the only way to know we do is to ask Go.

The cases cover every length up to 64, the shapes that push a quicksort into its slow paths, and the aliased comparator at the four lengths the original's mutated run count produces. The generator is `tools/gosort-vectors`. Regenerating needs Go and should not be necessary: the point of a fixture is that it stops moving.

`.gitattributes` marks this directory as binary so that a checkout on Windows does not rewrite the line endings and break every assertion in here.
